topic: A tornado is coming while you drive on the highway: is the overpass safe?
title: Tornado On The Highway
idea: The highway overpass looks like a roof but is a trap, not a shelter.
hook: A tornado is coming, and you're on the highway.

beats.line: An overpass ahead looks like the perfect roof.
beats.see: Car speeds toward a concrete bridge with the funnel behind it; a dotted 'SHELTER?' outline glows under the bridge. Outline on 'roof'.

beats.line: But wind under a bridge is usually faster.
beats.see: Wind arrows squeeze into the gap under the bridge and grow bigger and faster; a wind gauge needle jumps. Arrows grow on 'faster'.

beats.line: And you're a sitting target for flying debris.
beats.see: Character crouched under the bridge; boards, signs and a road cone fly straight through the gap at them. Debris on 'flying'.

beats.line: Oklahoma, nineteen ninety nine. Winds of about three hundred miles an hour.
beats.see: Date stamp MAY 3 1999 over an Oklahoma map; a radar dish reads a speed counter climbing to 300 MPH. Counter on 'three hundred'.

beats.line: Three people died under or near overpasses.
beats.see: Three small bridge icons appear on the map, each with a dark marker; parked cars are tossed out from under one. Icons on 'three', cars on 'overpasses'.
Tape rewinds: the car reverses out from the bridge back onto the open highway, funnel far away. Rewind on 'again'.

beats.line: One. Best is a basement or an inner room, not a car.
beats.see: Step card 1 REAL SHELTER; split house cutaway shows a basement and a windowless inner room glowing green, the car icon crossed out. Glow on 'basement', X on 'car'.

beats.line: Two. Stuck in the car? Stay buckled, head below the windows.
beats.see: Step card 2 BUCKLED, HEAD DOWN; seatbelt clicks and the character ducks below the window line as glass shards fly above. Click on 'buckled', duck on 'below'.

beats.line: Three. Or lie somewhere clearly lower than the road, covering your head.
beats.see: Step card 3 LIE LOW; character lies in a low spot beside the road, arms over head, with a dashed line showing the road level above them. Line on 'lower', arms on 'covering'.

end.line: Rewatch it. That overpass won't look like a roof again.
end.see: Save card with the three steps (REAL SHELTER, BUCKLED HEAD DOWN, LIE LOW); the overpass in the background gets a red TRAP stamp. Card on 'Rewatch', stamp on 'roof', loops to the hook highway.

description: A tornado is coming and you're on the highway. The overpass looks safe. It's a trap.

facts.claim: Highway overpasses are not shelters: wind speeds are typically higher there and you are a stationary target for flying debris.
On 3 May 1999 in Oklahoma three people were killed under or near overpasses.
Strongest tornado wind ever measured: about 300 mph (NSSL gives 318 mph), by mobile Doppler radar, Bridge Creek-Moore, Oklahoma, 3 May 1999.

Go to a basement or safe room, else an interior room away from windows; a car is not safe. If caught in a car: stay buckled, head down below the windows, or lie in a spot clearly lower than the road; cover head and neck.

notes: 'Usually faster' paraphrases NWS 'wind speeds are typically higher'; the see field shows wind squeezing into the gap as illustration only, the script does not explain a mechanism. The 300 mph figure was measured in the same outbreak (Bridge Creek-Moore), not necessarily at the overpasses; the line only says 'Oklahoma, 1999. Winds of about 300 mph', keep the radar graphic separate from the bridge icons. No lead-time numbers, no window-opening myth. Big number: about three hundred miles an hour.
